note: The campaign's declared rows and the carriage names their UDP traffic is judged by, as machine-readable rules.
This file is the rule source of benchmarks/WinForward.E2E/scripts/check-fairness.py, which asserts the C#
analysis's own output against it; a row, a carriage name or a label that changes here without changing the
analysis (or the other way round) turns that checker red, because the expected answer is read from this file
and the actual answer from the produced tables.md.
The same declarations live in the analysis's own source (Model/RowProfiles.cs); the checker is what keeps the
two honest, and the report's section 1 is generated from the analysis's copy.

udp53.direct-local-target: direct via the local DNS target (udp/53 forwarded verbatim, bypasses the proxy)
udp53.direct-hardcoded-bypass: direct via the product's hardcoded port-53 pass-through
udp53.direct-not-carried: direct (the product cannot carry UDP at all)
udp53.n/a: n/a (no product loaded: the direct path is the only path)

wf-aot-opt.config: UDP-over-TCP v2 on, DNS local target on (reference configuration)

wf-aot-nativeudp.config: UDP-over-TCP off, everything else identical to wf-aot-opt

wf-aot-dnsrelay.config: DNS local target off, everything else identical to wf-aot-opt

proxifyre.config: SOCKS5 rule for the client, supportedProtocols TCP+UDP

proxifier.config: SOCKS5 profile, process rules (no UDP support in the product)

proxybridge.config: PROXY rule for the client, DIRECT rule for sing-box

control-pre.product: none (control block before the product block)

control-post.product: none (control block after the product block)
